title: The Slough of Despond
hook: Christian sinks in a bog of discouragement, and Help pulls him out
tomorrow: why does a book about a long walk end with trumpets?

segments.voice: Last week closed on Pascal's memorial: joy, joy, tears of joy. This week opens on the other kind of day, and a book written as a dream.
screen: `JOY, JOY, TEARS OF JOY.` → `THE OTHER KIND OF DAY.`

segments.voice: Two travelers on a flat plain, deep in conversation about the shining city ahead, so busy talking that nobody watches the ground. Then John Bunyan writes, in The Pilgrim's Progress, that they, being heedless, "did both fall suddenly into the bog. The name of the slough was Despond." Mud to the waist. The one called Pliable struggles out on the side nearest his own house, and goes home. The other, called Christian, is left alone, sinking, with a heavy burden on his back. He tries for the far bank and can't reach it. A traveler sinks in a bog called Despond. Who pulls him out?
screen: `DEEP IN CONVERSATION.` → `THE NAME OF THE SLOUGH WAS DESPOND.` → `ONE GOES HOME. ONE IS SINKING.`

segments.voice: A man walks up. Bunyan gives him the plainest name in the book: Help. He asks Christian what he's doing there. Christian explains he was on his way, and fell in. Help asks, in effect, why didn't you look for the steps? There are good steps laid right through the middle of the bog. And Christian's answer is honest: fear chased him so hard he ran the nearest way, and fell in. Then no lecture. Help says, "Give me thy hand," draws him out, and, in Bunyan's words, sets him "upon sound ground," and sends him on his way. Bunyan explains the slough, too. It's where the fears and doubts that come with waking up to your own life drain down and collect. It can't be paved over, though workers have tried. The steps are there; in the murk, people miss them. So despond is the old word for losing heart, and Bunyan puts it on the road, not at the end. One to tell a friend tonight: the first traveler out of the mud wasn't rescued. He just turned back.
screen: `A MAN NAMED HELP.` · `WHY DIDN'T YOU LOOK FOR THE STEPS?` · `GIVE ME THY HAND.` · `ON THE ROAD, NOT THE END.` · then, large: `HELP PULLED HIM OUT.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who's stuck in a bog right now: a hard semester, a long illness, a loss. Send them a few words that ask nothing back, a hand held out rather than advice. If you pray, hold their name for the rest of the sit.
The Slough of Despond. Bunyan's bog of discouragement, out in the middle of the road, with steps people miss and a man named Help.
Your line: help pulled him out. Not a speech; a hand, and sound ground. Talk tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Pilgrim's Progress has long been read in Christian homes and churches as a picture of the life of faith; readers use its places, like the Slough of Despond, to name stretches of their own road.

fork.setup: your friend failed her driving test twice and says she's done trying. you passed last month. what does Help do in Bunyan's story?
options: reaches out a hand, sets her on solid ground, and sends her on.
explains exactly where she went wrong so it won't happen again.

fork.reveal: Help does ask one question about the steps, but then no lecture: give me thy hand, sound ground, and on your way.
